sentences.text: Tenuicruris piscanexum represents a newly described enantiornithean bird from the Early Cretaceous Albian Toolebuc Formation of Australia.
It is only the second Mesozoic bird to receive a formal name from Australia.
The holotype, catalogued as KK F1451, consists of a nearly complete left tibiotarsus and is stored at the Kronosaurus Korner Museum.
The bone was recovered about 12 km northwest of Richmond, Queensland, at the public fossicking area Dig Site 1, and the species was formally described by Matt A. White and colleagues in 2026.
The preserved tibiotarsus measures 6.54 cm in length, roughly double the comparable bone length in the coeval Nanantius (3.14 cm).
A pronounced craniolateral cnemial crest—a ridge on the front-side of the shin bone—appears, a trait also observed in the Chinese enantiornitheans Monoenantiornis and Qiliania.
